name: rt_sigaction
synopsis: int sigaction(int signum, const struct sigaction *_Nullable restrict act, struct sigaction *_Nullable restrict oldact);
description: The rt_sigaction system call examines and changes the action taken by a process on receipt of a specific signal. It allows installing a new signal handler and optionally saving the previous one.

parameters.name: signum
parameters.description: The signal number, which must be a valid signal except SIGKILL and SIGSTOP.

parameters.name: act
parameters.description: Pointer to a sigaction structure that specifies the new action for the signal, or NULL if no new action is to be set.

parameters.name: oldact
parameters.description: Pointer to a sigaction structure where the previous action is stored, or NULL if not needed.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: act or oldact points to memory which is not a valid part of the process address space
An invalid signal was specified, or an attempt is made to change the action for SIGKILL or SIGSTOP

bugs: Support for new flags in sa_flags cannot be reliably probed, as unknown bits may not be cleared properly in older kernels, potentially leading to inconsistent behavior.
